extracted.intended_audience: general public, journalists, researchers, and fans interested in American comedy awards and the Kennedy Center's Mark Twain Prize
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the standards, purpose, selection process, and ceremonial/eligibility practices that govern awarding the Mark Twain Prize for American Humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose / eligibility phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented to individuals who have "had an impact on American society in ways similar to" Mark Twain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the stated award rationale used by the Kennedy Center; the exact quoted language appears in the article as the primary articulation of who the prize is meant to honor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: honor greatest contributors to American comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of the prize is "to honor the greatest contributors to American comedy of our time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement (attributed to co-founder/producer Cappy McGarr) frames the prize as a lifetime/contribution award recognizing major contributors to American comedy and culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary substantive criterion: lifetime career and influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary criteria is "to choose people who've had a full lifetime of making us laugh and who've had a great influence on the people who've followed them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted from McGarr; emphasizes both sustained career (a 'full lifetime' of work) and demonstrable influence on subsequent comedians/industry as key evaluative factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for living recipients (not intended posthumously)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kennedy Center's intent is to give the award to living persons (the award is not intended to be given posthumously).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical exceptions exist (e.g., George Carlin died after announcement but before ceremony). Historically the prize is awarded to living honorees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: honors American humor, not necessarily American-born humorists
rubrics_metrics.description: In awarding the prize to Lorne Michaels in 2004, McGarr explained that "the Mark Twain Prize honors American humor, not necessarily American humorists."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prize can recognize non-U.S.-born individuals whose work is considered part of American humor (example: Lorne Michaels, Canadian‑American).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process: shortlist and decision-making structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A short list is compiled by the executive producers and presented to a group comprised of representatives from the Kennedy Center board of trustees, as well as the Kennedy Center senior management and programming staff; decision-making described as a consensus decision among executive producers in consultation with the chairman and president.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes 'little is known' publicly about the process but gives this procedural outline: executive producers generate short list, group of trustees/management reviews, and executive producers (McGarr, Mark Krantz, Peter and Bob Kaminsky) decide in consultation with the Kennedy Center leadership. Quoted language: "there's really no committee... It's really a consensus decision."

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremony format and presentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of Karl Gerhardt's 1884 bust of Twain is presented in a ceremony usually in the Kennedy Center Concert Hall, during which the recipient is celebrated by his or her peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ceremony is typically a large, peer-salute event that serves as a significant fundraiser for the Kennedy Center, including ticket sales, dinners and after-parties; honorees are celebrated by fellow comedians and celebrities (many examples listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcasting and scheduling practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize is presented annually since 1998 (except 2020–2021); broadcasts have been handled by various networks (Comedy Central 1998–1999, PBS 2000–2022, CNN 2023, Netflix 2024–present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows a pattern of annual scheduling and changing media partnerships; the pandemic produced a two-year hiatus (2020–2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive eligibility across comedy professions
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees have included a writer, an actor, a producer, a stand-up comedian and a media proprietor, among others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prize recognizes contributions across multiple comedy-related professions and formats, not limited to one performance medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential meeting customary but optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Since Carl Reiner, honorees are given the opportunity to meet the president, although some refuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a customary optional component of the honoree experience rather than an eligibility criterion; some recipients decline the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission for misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards can be rescinded in light of serious misconduct (example: Bill Cosby's award was rescinded by the Kennedy Center in 2018 after his conviction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article documents that the Kennedy Center has revoked honors in response to post-award revelations and legal findings, indicating moral/conduct considerations can affect award status.
